task.description: HARD GATE. Run WF-02 Step 2d against this run's diff (git diff origin/main...HEAD, implementation commit 2fe967f) using .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions: idiomatic OTP vs. crutch, supervision integrity, type-safety gaps, and scope creep -- plus consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ and docs/anti-patterns.md. Three specific rulings are wanted, each stated explicitly with reasoning rather than left implicit: (1) whether the change to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex is genuine Unblock-Everything scope or scope creep against REQ-023; (2) whether the Code.require_file / ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2 approach is idiomatic Elixir or a crutch, given it exists to work around priv/repo/migrations not being on elixirc_paths; (3) whether the disclosed divergence of event_payload_store.payload to jsonb (:map), against REQ-023's own looser 'text/bytea' phrasing, is acceptable and properly justified.
acceptance_criteria: the diff is reviewed against reviewer.md's four questions, each answered explicitly
consistency with docs/migration/decisions/0003 (Decisions A, B, C) is checked and stated
docs/anti-patterns.md is checked against this diff
the three specific rulings above are each given with reasoning
non-blocking findings are recorded rather than silently dropped

result.summary: PASS. Reviewed `git diff origin/main...HEAD` on feature/WF02-REQ023-20260816 (implementation commit 2fe967f: six migrations 20260816120001-120006, six Ecto.Schema modules under lib/letflow/event_store/, and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex). Verdict is re-derived from the artefacts and from executed commands, not from ELIXIR-DEV's or SECURITY-REVIEWER's self-reports. Toolchain was available (Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29), so nothing below is speculation. COMMANDS ACTUALLY RUN: (i) `MIX_ENV=dev mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> exit 0, 'Compiling 7 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app'; (ii) `mix format --check-formatted` -> exit 0; (iii) a fresh-VM probe `MIX_ENV=dev mix run --no-start -e ...` printing BEFORE ensure_loaded?: [false, false, false] / AFTER ensure_loaded?: [true, true, true], the six {version, module} tuples in ascending order 20260816120001..120006 matching their filename prefixes, `function_exported?(mod, :__migration__, 0)` true for all six, and a second call returning an identical list with no 'redefining module' warning; (iv) a throwaway-schema DDL probe in letflow_test2 (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 partition; schema rev2d_probe created and dropped, letflow_test / letflow_dev untouched) confirming that the exact SQL Ecto emits for migration 4 is accepted by Postgres -- the composite FK is declared before `event_created_at` is declared in the same CREATE TABLE and still resolves, `pg_get_constraintdef` reads 'FOREIGN KEY (event_id, event_created_at) REFERENCES rev2d_probe.events(event_id, created_at) ON DELETE RESTRICT' inside the non-public schema, and `:bigserial` lands its sequence in the tenant schema as `events_global_seq_seq`, exactly as 20260816120001_create_events.exs:51-58 states. || FOUR QUESTIONS. (1) IDIOMATIC vs. CRUTCH -- idiomatic, no crutch found. All six migrations use the Ecto.Migration DSL end to end (`create table(..., primary_key: false, prefix: prefix())`, `unique_index`/`index` with explicit `name:`, `references/2` with `:with` for the composite FK, `timestamps/1` using only documented options); there is no `execute/1` and no raw SQL anywhere in the six files, so REQ-023 introduces zero identifier interpolation (INV-EV-13 holds). Options used were verified against the shipped deps, not assumed: `on_delete: :restrict` is legal at deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migration.ex:1590, `:with` is documented at :1552, and a %Reference{} carrying no :prefix falls back to the referencing table's own prefix at deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/postgres/connection.ex:1872 -- so the FK stays inside the tenant schema, as the migration header claims. Schema modules are plain `use Ecto.Schema` + Ecto.Changeset with `Ecto.Enum` in its keyword-mapping form (instance_projection.ex:48-51, preserving R-Co's uppercase DB values) and `read_after_writes: true` on the DB-assigned global_seq (event.ex:78); every public function has a @doc and a @spec, and the shape matches the repo's existing lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex convention exactly (parenthesised `field(...)`, `Ecto.UUID`, `@primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}`, `@type t :: %__MODULE__{}`). The `if prefix() do ... end` guard is the one construct that could read as a workaround, but it is not hand-rolling anything Ecto provides -- Ecto has no 'tenant-only migration' declaration, `Ecto.Migration.prefix/0` is the public accessor for exactly this, REQ-022's design mandated the shape, and test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex:24-30 is the shipped reference; all six follow it identically with a genuine no-op nil branch. Immutability by omission of `update_changeset/2` (Event, ArchivedEvent, InstanceSequence, StoredPayload, IdempotencyRecord all expose only `insert_changeset/2`) is the idiomatic Elixir answer and is what 0003 Decision C point 1 prescribes. See ruling (2) for `ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2`. (2) SUPERVISION -- intact, confirmed rather than assumed. `git diff --name-only` shows lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/process_instance.ex, lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex and lib/letflow/approval_supervisor.ex are all absent from the diff. A grep for GenServer|gen_statem|Supervisor|spawn|Task\.|Agent|start_link|Process\.|:ets|send\(|receive across lib/letflow/event_store/ and all six migrations returned zero hits: the diff adds no process of any kind, so per-instance supervised isolation is untouched. The only runtime-behaviour change in the whole diff is that `tenant_scoped_migrations/0` now performs `Code.require_file/1`; that call serialises through Elixir's code server, so two tenants provisioning concurrently cannot double-define a module, and it is six small files once per VM. (3) TYPE-SAFETY GAPS -- five recorded, all non-blocking, in result.issues #3-#7: field-typeless `@type t :: %__MODULE__{}` on all six modules leaves `insert_changeset(t(), map())` opaque to Dialyzer and lets `cast/3` silently drop a mistyped optional key such as :metadata; INV-EV-5's one-event_id-bound-everywhere invariant is enforced at the DB only for events<->event_payload_store (the composite FK) and by nothing at all for events<->event_idempotency, which correctly has no FK -- R-Co shipped precisely that bug (store.zig:623-636, cited in event.ex:28-38), and only a REQ-025 property test can catch a regression; `InstanceProjection.terminal?/1` (instance_projection.ex:93-94) covers all four enum values in two guard clauses with no catch-all, so a fifth status raises FunctionClauseError at runtime where an exhaustive-match type system would fail at compile time (loud-not-silent, so the right trade here, but undocumented as deliberate); the manifest's version integer and filename prefix are two independent facts kept in sync only by a comment (tenant_provisioning.ex:183-186), and design §5.2 admits nothing catches a wrong-but-unique version; and the immutability invariant is API-surface convention only -- `Repo.update_all/2` or a raw query still bypasses it, which 0003 point 1 explicitly acknowledges Ecto cannot express in DDL. (4) SCOPE CREEP -- none found. The diff creates exactly the six tables REQ-023's title and description name (events, instance_sequence, event_payload_store, events_archive, the idempotency sidecar, instance_projections) and no seventh. No behaviour, no macro, no generic plumbing; no Letflow.EventStore context module (correctly left to REQ-025/026); the engine-owned instance_projections columns (definition_id, correlation_key, current_nodes, variables, error_detail, completed_at, cancelled_at and their two indexes) are explicitly enumerated as deferred to S3 rather than added early. EXCLUDING event_retention_policies WAS RIGHT: REQ-023's description does not list it, it is needed by REQ-026, and building it here would be exactly the 'framework machinery a stage hasn't reached' pattern reviewer.md question 4 names -- and it would ship a table whose columns no design gate approved. ISS-0013 is the correct disposition. `InstanceProjection.terminal?/1` is the only borderline addition; it is a three-line pure predicate over the enum this very migration defines, justified by design INV-EV-10 from a cited R-Co invariant (event_store.md:292), so it is a watch-item, not creep. || RULING 1 -- the tenant_provisioning.ex change is GENUINE UNBLOCK-EVERYTHING, NOT SCOPE CREEP. It has two halves and both survive the test. Half (a), registering the six {version, module} tuples, is not merely permitted but mandated: REQ-022's own shipped @doc says every tenant-scoped migration from REQ-023 onward must register here, design §1 lists the edit as in-scope, and REQ-023 acceptance criterion 1 requires the migrations to apply 'via REQ-022's migration-replay mechanism' -- with `tenant_scoped_migrations/0` still returning [] the default replay path would select nothing and AC1 would be unmeetable. Half (b), `ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2`, is the interesting one, and I tested ORCH's framing rather than accepting it. The defect is real and I re-derived it from source: `Ecto.Migrator.load_migration!/1` for the atom-module form (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migrator.ex:725-731) delegates to `migration?/1` (:744-746), which is `Code.ensure_loaded?(mod) and function_exported?(mod, :__migration__, 0)`; mix.exs:20-21 sets elixirc_paths to ["lib"] (plus test/support under :test), so no .beam exists for any priv/repo/migrations module. I then confirmed it empirically instead of arguing it: in a fresh VM with no in-process `mix ecto.migrate`, `Code.ensure_loaded?` was false for CreateEvents, CreateEventPayloadStore and CreateEventIdempotency before the call and true after -- i.e. without the fix `Ecto.Migrator.run/4` raises Ecto.MigrationError on the very first replay. Corroborating evidence that this was never previously exercised: REQ-022's only replay test passes `[{1, MigrationFixture}]`, and MigrationFixture lives in test/support/, which IS on elixirc_paths under :test -- so the shipped mechanism had only ever been driven with a compiled module. Applying core-directives.md's scope boundary: this is 'what stands in your way', not 'a defect you merely notice', because it blocks REQ-023's own acceptance criterion 1 on the default code path. I checked the obvious escape hatch and reject it: satisfying AC1 by passing an explicit pre-loaded migration_source in a test while leaving `tenant_scoped_migrations/0` at [] would demonstrate a mechanism production never uses and would leave the registration half undone, which REQ-022's @doc calls inert -- that is 'satisfy a gate by editing what it measures', not a fix. The fix is also minimal and non-invasive: one private function, one module attribute, both public @specs byte-identical, confined to the one function REQ-023 was already mandated to edit, and no destructive or irreversible change to unrelated functionality. Finally, the file-and-forward half was done correctly too: ISS-0017 records the documentation drift the fix leaves in REQ-022's design doc and test spec, explicitly declining to edit another requirement's already-gated design artefact from inside this run. That is the directive followed as written, in both directions. || RULING 2 -- `ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2` IS IDIOMATIC, NOT A CRUTCH. reviewer.md's crutch test is hand-rolling what the framework already provides, or fighting its grain. Neither applies. The {version, module} source is a first-class documented Ecto form (migrator.ex:669-670), and the contract Ecto attaches to that form is that the module be loaded; loading it is satisfying Ecto's contract, not bypassing it. The mechanism used is Ecto's own: `load_migration!/1` reaches for `Code.compile_file/1` on the directory form at :733-742, and the diff uses `Code.require_file/1`, the same operation with the code server's idempotency lock -- strictly the more careful of the two, and guarded by `Code.ensure_loaded?/1` so an in-VM `mix ecto.migrate` that already compiled the file is not redefined. Ten lines, private, no public @spec change, and empirically correct in a fresh VM. On the rejected directory-source alternative (design §2.4/§5.2) I AGREE, having checked the reasons rather than taking them: reason (a) holds -- the directory form would widen `tenant_scoped_migrations/0`'s return to [binary] and change `replay_migrations/2`'s second-argument @spec, i.e. a public-contract change to already-merged, already-gated REQ-022 code, which is more invasive than the loading fix, not less; reason (b) holds and I verified it independently -- `migrations_for/1` globs `Path.join([directory, "**", "*.{ex,exs}"])` at migrator.ex:663-665, so a nested priv/repo/migrations/tenant/ subdirectory is still swept up by a plain `mix ecto.migrate` and the §2.2 guard stays mandatory either way, meaning the subdirectory buys literally no isolation; reason (c) is directionally right but imprecise, and I have recorded that as issue #6 -- 'redefining module' from `Code.compile_file/1` is a runtime code-server warning, not a compiler diagnostic, so `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` would not turn it into a failure, though the underlying point (recompiling six files once per tenant provisioning is avoidable work and real log noise) stands. Since (a) and (b) each independently carry the decision, the conclusion is sound even with (c) discounted. I also considered the alternative the design did not name, adding priv/repo/migrations to elixirc_paths, and it is decisively worse: it would make every migration a permanent compiled release artefact and put compiled modules in conflict with the `Code.compile_file` the directory form (used by plain `mix ecto.migrate` and by the {Ecto.Migrator, ...} child at application.ex:14-15) performs on the same files, besides being contrary to universal Ecto convention. The one mildly crutch-shaped residue is the manifest's unguarded version/filename redundancy, recorded as non-blocking issue #1. || RULING 3 -- THE event_payload_store.payload DIVERGENCE IS JUSTIFIED AND PROPERLY RECORDED; NO REQUIREMENT AMENDMENT WAS NEEDED. REQ-023's description offers 'payload (text/bytea)' -- a slash-separated pair, i.e. the requirement text itself never settled on one type, exactly as it writes 'payload (text/jsonb ...)' for the events table where nobody disputes jsonb. I read all five acceptance criteria: none constrains the payload type (they cover the six migrations' existence + :prefix + clean application, the composite PK, events' immutability, the sidecar's unique index and moduledoc, and instance_projections' moduledoc), so the divergence cannot fail any criterion. I opened both cited R-Co files rather than trusting the citation: migrations/012_event_retention.sql:19 reads `payload JSONB NOT NULL` and 1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql:219 reads `payload JSONB NOT NULL` -- both revisions, no exception. That makes jsonb R-Co's actual type, so under 0003 Decision A (preserve R-Co's meaning, redesign only the authoring idiom) choosing text/bytea would have been the divergence, not jsonb. There is also a real correctness argument, not merely a preference: events.payload is :map/jsonb and design INV-EV-6 requires the large-payload split to be invisible above the append/read layer, with REQ-026 splicing the side-table value back into that same field; a text or bytea side table would force an encode/decode across the splice and muddy INV-EV-7's byte_size semantics further. On whether an amendment was owed first: an amendment is warranted when a criterion cannot be met as written or a decision record is contradicted, and neither holds -- Decision A actively favours the choice. core-directives.md's decision-draft exception (two genuinely equivalent options needing a preference no agent can infer) also does not apply, because this one IS inferable from 0003 plus R-Co, so filing a draft would have been the wrong move. Disclosure is in three places, none of them hidden: the migration header at 20260816120004_create_event_payload_store.exs:46-47, design §3.4, and ELIXIR-DEV's handoff. One forward-looking limitation is recorded as issue #7 (jsonb is not byte-transparent, so this table cannot round-trip an opaque non-JSON blob the way bytea could -- nothing today needs that, but the reason should be findable if something later does). || DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY (0003) -- no silent contradiction found; nothing needs CLAUDE.md sign-off. Decision A: binary_id everywhere it applies -- event_payload_store and event_idempotency carry binary_id surrogate `id` PKs, and the three exceptions (events'/events_archive' composite (event_id, created_at); instance_sequence's and instance_projections' natural instance_id PKs) are the exceptions REQ-023's own text names. The TEXT-status-to-Ecto.Enum swap is present (instance_projection.ex:48-51). R-Co names are preserved, with exactly two divergences, both argued from Decision A's own text rather than asserted: dropping the `plat_` prefix (R-Co's par-01-monthly-range-partitioning.md:203-209 flags that table as an exception to its own prefix convention) and `event_created_at` vs `created_at` (R-Co uses one name for two different meanings across revisions -- design §10 contradiction C-3). Decision B: :prefix used on every table and every index in all six migrations, and no schema module carries @schema_prefix (INV-EV-8), which is correct because these tables live in many schemas. tenant_id is retained intra-schema on events, events_archive and instance_projections and absent on instance_sequence, event_payload_store and event_idempotency. I checked whether that asymmetry contradicts Decision B and it does not: Decision B's own wording scopes retention to 'the tables the adp-0x docs describe', and R-Co agrees -- 027_adp01_event_store_tenant.sql adds tenant_id to exactly events and events_archive, and R-Co actively DROPS tenant_id from instance_sequence in GBL-116_tnt07_rls_cleanup.sql:117, GBL-123:91, GBL-130:121 and GBL-131:90. So the split matches both the decision and upstream; what is missing is only a sentence saying so, recorded as non-blocking issue #2. Decision C: point 1 satisfied (no update path on any event table; InstanceProjection's update_changeset/2 is legitimate because point 3 classes projections as ordinary CRUD tables); point 2(a) satisfied on both events and events_archive; point 2(b) satisfied -- event_idempotency carries uq_event_idempotency_key and I confirmed by reading both migrations that neither events nor events_archive declares any unique index on idempotency_key, so there is exactly one enforcement point; point 3 satisfied; partitioning correctly absent (no PARTITION BY anywhere); and all six event-store tables use the same schema-per-tenant mechanism as everything else, including the sidecar, per 0003's closing paragraph. || ANTI-PATTERNS (docs/anti-patterns.md, both entries) -- neither violated. Entry 1 (no toolchain -> use the Docker fallback, do not stop at 'can't verify'): not triggered and not evaded; the toolchain was present and I ran real commands and quoted real output, so nothing in this verdict rests on speculation. Entry 2 (overwriting requirement_status.yaml instead of appending): `git diff origin/main...HEAD --numstat` shows docs/status/requirement_status.yaml at 18 added / 0 deleted and handoffs/orchestrator.log at 15 added / 0 deleted -- both strictly append-only; handoffs/registry.json is 74/16 (net +58, ORCH-owned entry-status updates, not a shrink); docs/requirements.yaml is a single line, REQ-023 pending -> in_progress. File Placement Rules are respected -- no stray file in the project root, and every new file is under lib/letflow/event_store/, priv/repo/migrations/, lib/letflow/design/, docs/issues/ or handoffs/. Handoff hygiene for this run also checked per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL's enforcement note: all six handoffs are schema-conformant with legal result.status values and monotonic timestamps, no completed_at preceding its started_at. || CROSS-REFERENCE: ISS-0019 (already filed by SECURITY-REVIEWER) correctly identifies that `replay_migrations/2`'s default argument is evaluated outside its own try/rescue, so a `Code.require_file` failure would escape as a raw exception instead of the @spec'd {:error, {:migration_failed, _}}. I independently confirm that reading of the code and concur with MINOR; it is not blocking because the file paths are a compile-time constant manifest, not external input. Not re-filed. || VERDICT: PASS. No genuine crutch, no broken supervision, no scope creep. Nine non-blocking findings recorded in result.issues rather than dropped; items #1, #2, #6 and #7 are new to this run and are NOT among ISS-0012..ISS-0019.

issues.description: NEW. @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:191-204) stores the version integer and the filename as two independent facts kept in sync only by the comment at :183-186 ('The version integers MUST equal the filenames' timestamp prefixes'). The version is literally derivable from the filename prefix, so the redundancy is unchecked: a future entry can transcribe a wrong-but-unique version and nothing catches it -- design §5.2 admits this ('it cannot catch a wrong-but-unique version'; Ecto.Migrator only raises on duplicate versions, migrator.ex:708-721). Not blocking: all six current entries were verified correct by direct execution. Suggested disposition: TEST-DESIGNER adds a cheap guard test asserting, for every entry of tenant_scoped_migrations/0, that the version equals the leading integer of its migration filename -- naturally paired with the §4-prefix()-guard-pattern test that ISS-0017's forward note already carries to Step 3.

NEW. tenant_id is present on events, events_archive and instance_projections but absent on instance_sequence, event_payload_store and event_idempotency, and neither the design artefact nor any migration header states why. This is NOT a divergence from 0003 Decision B -- I verified the split is correct on two independent grounds: Decision B scopes tenant_id retention to 'the tables the adp-0x docs describe', and R-Co's own schema agrees (migrations/027_adp01_event_store_tenant.sql adds tenant_id to exactly events and events_archive; R-Co then actively drops it from instance_sequence at GBL-116_tnt07_rls_cleanup.sql:117, GBL-123:91, GBL-130:121 and GBL-131:90). The gap is purely that the reasoning is unrecorded, so a future reader cannot tell a decision from an oversight. Suggested disposition: one sentence in the design's §3.2/§3.4/§3.5 column tables next time REQ-025 touches these files. No rework of this diff needed.

Type-safety gap (reviewer.md question 3). All six new modules declare `@type t :: %__MODULE__{}` with no field types, so `@spec insert_changeset(t(), attrs :: map())` tells Dialyzer nothing about attrs: a mistyped key is silently dropped by cast/3, surfacing as a validate_required error for required fields and as nothing at all for optional ones (e.g. :metadata on Event/ArchivedEvent). A stricter type system would reject the call site at compile time. This matches the repo's established convention (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex and the five lib/letflow/identity/ schemas do the same), so it is consistency, not a regression -- but this diff makes it eleven-plus modules and worth watching as the schema grows, which is exactly the kind of pattern reviewer.md asks to be flagged.

Type-safety gap, forward to TEST-DESIGNER and REQ-025. Design INV-EV-5 requires one event_id and one created_at to be minted once and bound byte-identically into events, event_idempotency and (for large payloads) event_payload_store. The composite FK enforces the events<->event_payload_store half at the database level, but the events<->event_idempotency half has no enforcement of any kind -- correctly, since that table deliberately carries no FK (the event may legitimately move to events_archive). R-Co shipped exactly this bug and had to fix it (src/event_store/store.zig:623-636, cited in lib/letflow/event_store/event.ex:28-38). Nothing in the schema layer, and no type system, can catch it; only a REQ-025 property test asserting the three rows share one event_id/created_at can. Recorded so Step 3 does not have to rediscover it.

Type-safety gap (reviewer.md question 3). Letflow.EventStore.InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 (lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex:93-94) covers all four Ecto.Enum values in two guard clauses with no catch-all. If a fifth status is added to the enum without updating this function, the result is a runtime FunctionClauseError where an exhaustive-match type system (Rust/OCaml) would fail the build. Loud-not-silent is the right trade under Elixir and is very likely deliberate, but it is nowhere documented as deliberate -- a one-line comment saying the absent catch-all is intentional would stop a future contributor from 'fixing' it with a `def terminal?(_), do: false` default, which would silently misclassify a new terminal status.

NEW. Accuracy defect in the design artefact's own reasoning, not in the code. lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md §2.4 rejects the directory-source alternative partly on reason (c), that Code.compile_file/1's 'redefining module' output would be 'noisy' under `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` discipline. Those are runtime warnings emitted by the code server, not compiler diagnostics, so --warnings-as-errors would not turn them into a failure; the stated mechanism is wrong even though the underlying observation (recompiling six files once per tenant provisioning is avoidable work and real log noise) is fair. This does not change the outcome -- I verified reasons (a) and (b) independently and each carries the rejection on its own -- so no rework is warranted. Recorded so the imprecision is not inherited by a future CODE-DESIGNER quoting §2.4.

NEW, forward-looking. jsonb is not byte-transparent: it normalises whitespace and key order and drops duplicate keys. Consequently event_payload_store (payload :map -> jsonb) cannot round-trip an opaque non-JSON or byte-exact blob, which the requirement text's alternative `bytea` could have. Nothing in REQ-023 through REQ-026 needs that -- payloads are JSON events -- and the design already records the visible consequence as INV-EV-7 (byte_size is the pre-storage length, not octet_length of the stored jsonb; lib/letflow/event_store/stored_payload.ex:12-18). What is not stated anywhere is the limitation itself. Recorded so that if a later requirement ever needs a byte-exact payload, the reason this table cannot serve it is findable without re-deriving it. Does not affect ruling 3, which is that the jsonb choice is correct and justified.

Empirical confirmation of the already-filed ISS-0016, plus an explicit do-not-do instruction. `mix format --check-formatted "priv/repo/migrations/2026081612000*.exs"` exits 1 for all six new files, solely because .formatter.exs lacks `import_deps: [:ecto_sql]` and so does not know Ecto.Migration's locals_without_parens: the only diff it proposes is parenthesising `add :instance_id, :binary_id, primary_key: true` into `add(:instance_id, ...)`. The project gate itself is green (`mix format --check-formatted` exits 0) because .formatter.exs's inputs never match priv/. IMPORTANT: nobody should 'fix' this by reformatting the migration files -- the parenthesised form is less idiomatic for Ecto migrations and diverges from every existing migration in this repo. The fix belongs to ISS-0016 (add import_deps and widen inputs), not to this diff.

Forward guard for TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3) and REQ-026. event_payload_store's foreign key uses `on_delete: :restrict` (priv/repo/migrations/20260816120004_create_event_payload_store.exs:71), deliberately diverging from R-Co's ON DELETE CASCADE, so that REQ-026's archive path fails loudly rather than silently destroying the side-table payload of every archived large event (design OQ-2 / INV-EV-12; rationale in the migration header at :25-34 and in lib/letflow/event_store/stored_payload.ex:28-44). That means REQ-026's first integration test against a large-payload event is EXPECTED to hit a restrict violation. That failure is the designed signal that OQ-2 is still open -- it must be resolved by deciding how payloads travel to the archive, and must NOT be 'fixed' by flipping the FK to CASCADE, which would reintroduce the data-loss path this diff closed. I concur with the divergence and with keeping it.
